nodes.label: Private Multi-AZ EKS Reference Topology
nodes.rationale: Terraform manages VPC, subnets, private EKS endpoint, dedicated system and repair node groups, RDS, S3/KMS, ECR, ACM, and Route 53, but receives secret ARNs and never secret values; the Helm chart references only Kubernetes Secrets, and no implicit cluster-creator admin back door exists.

nodes.label: Signed-Digest Deploy Workflow
nodes.rationale: Accepts only repository@sha256 digest inputs verified with Cosign against the release workflow identity, exchanges GitHub OIDC for a short-lived AWS role, rehearses migrations on an isolated database, canaries through a private port-forward, and rolls back to the captured Helm revision on failure; tags, latest, public registries, and long-lived AWS keys are rejected, and production approval is a required human gate.

nodes.label: Two-Phase Terraform/Helm Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: The first deployment is deliberately two-phase because an ALB hostname does not exist before the chart creates its ingress; Terraform is applied with an empty hostname, the chart is installed, then Terraform is reapplied with the observed ALB hostname.

nodes.label: Warm DR Region and Operator-Authorized Promotion
nodes.rationale: Multi-AZ is not regional failover; DR promotion is operator-authorized and requires fencing the former writer, integrity and idempotency validation before any Route 53 change, and a preserved failback path. Rehearsal wrappers must never point at production.

nodes.label: Repair Pod Isolation (gVisor)
nodes.rationale: Repair pods run under a gVisor RuntimeClass on isolated nodes with no host filesystem, container socket, cloud role, service-account token, or metadata endpoint, so a malicious repair candidate cannot reach the host or cloud account.
